definition: A function is specified in natural language, compiled by a neural compiler into a small parameter-efficient adapter (weights), and executed by a frozen interpreter. The resulting artifact is reusable, locally executable, and cheaper than direct prompting of a large model.
supported_by_fulltext: S120-001 demonstrates the PAW compiler/interpreter pair and FuzzyBench; S120-002 shows that linearised attention can be viewed as fast-weight programming; S120-004 surveys weight-space learning as a structured domain; S120-007 shows that neural networks can induce latent programs from weak supervision.
not_supported_by_fulltext: No source provides a formal specification language, equivalence checker, or effect system for PAW functions. The results are empirical and domain-specific.

node_relevance.1 FunctionSpec: PARTIAL — natural language spec only, no formal contract
node_relevance.4 Artifact: STRONG — small adapter is the artifact
node_relevance.6 ExecutionTrace: PARTIAL — execution is differentiable but not externally traceable

readjudication_summary: FP-121-001 is a real and promising paradigm, but it is not a drop-in solution for all ignition function requirements. It lacks formal specification, equivalence checking, and effect tracking.

definition: A hypernetwork (a smaller neural network) generates the weights of a main network conditioned on an embedding or task context. This decouples function specification from the final parameter tensor.
supported_by_fulltext: S120-009 introduces hypernetworks for CNNs and LSTMs; S120-010 reviews hypernetworks across continual learning, federated learning, and transfer learning; S120-011 uses a central hypernetwork to generate personalized client models in federated learning.
not_supported_by_fulltext: Hypernetworks do not provide a formal semantics for the generated function, nor do they solve equivalence checking or weight-space composition. They are typically trained end-to-end for a specific task family.

node_relevance.2 Representation: STRONG — generated weights as function representation
node_relevance.4 Artifact: STRONG — generated weights are the artifact
node_relevance.8 ComposerRouter: PARTIAL — conditional generation can be seen as routing

readjudication_summary: FP-121-002 is well-established for weight generation and conditional adaptation. It does not, by itself, provide a full Function OS stack.

definition: A program is synthesized from a specification (natural language, I/O examples, pseudocode) and validated by execution. Execution signals guide search or generation.
supported_by_fulltext: S120-017 uses latent execution for C program synthesis; S120-018 searches pseudocode-to-code with compilation and test feedback; S120-020 decomposes algorithms into hierarchical NL descriptions and searches over implementations; S120-021 guides generation with line-by-line execution signals; S120-022 extends reasoning via pseudo-program emulation and search.
not_supported_by_fulltext: These systems are for code generation, not general function specification. They do not address weight-space artifacts, equivalence checking, or effect tracking.

node_relevance.1 FunctionSpec: PARTIAL — specs are natural language or I/O pairs

readjudication_summary: FP-121-003 is mature for code synthesis but remains focused on source-code artifacts. It provides a strong validation and execution model that can inform the Function OS, but not the weight-space representation layer.

definition: Functions are learned as operators between Banach spaces of functions, typically for PDEs. A single neural operator represents an entire family of equations/parameters.
supported_by_fulltext: S120-027 provides approximation-theoretic foundations for neural operators; S120-030 introduces the Fourier Neural Operator and demonstrates zero-shot super-resolution and speedups over classical solvers.
not_supported_by_fulltext: Neural operators are specialized to PDE-like function-space maps. They do not provide a general-purpose function specification, composition algebra, or effect system.

node_relevance.1 FunctionSpec: PARTIAL — PDE parameter family is implicit
node_relevance.2 Representation: STRONG — operator maps between function spaces
node_relevance.3 Compiler: PARTIAL — training is the compilation process
node_relevance.4 Artifact: STRONG — trained operator is the artifact

readjudication_summary: FP-121-004 is a rigorous mathematical paradigm for PDEs. It is not directly applicable to general computational functions, but its function-space view informs the representation layer.

definition: Functions are represented as small low-rank adapter weights added to a frozen base model. Multiple adapters can be stored, retrieved, and composed for different tasks.
supported_by_fulltext: S120-035 introduces LoRA; S120-031 routes and composes LoRA adapters via task representations; S120-036 composes adapters via vector-database retrieval and merging; S120-075 (MAML) prepares models for fast adaptation in weight space.
not_supported_by_fulltext: Adapter composition is heuristic and empirically validated. There is no formal guarantee of compositional correctness, no equivalence checker, and no effect system.

node_relevance.1 FunctionSpec: PARTIAL — task is implicit, no formal contract
node_relevance.2 Representation: STRONG — low-rank matrices as function representation
node_relevance.8 ComposerRouter: STRONG — routing/composition is the main focus

readjudication_summary: FP-121-005 is the closest practical paradigm to a versioned, composable function registry. It is strong on nodes 4, 8, and 9, but weak on formal specification and equivalence.

definition: Functions represented as weight checkpoints are combined by averaging, addition, negation, or sign-aware merging to produce a new model.
supported_by_fulltext: S120-039 averages fine-tuned model weights (model soups); S120-045 defines task vectors and performs addition/negation/analogy in weight space; S120-046 resolves sign and redundancy interference during merging.
not_supported_by_fulltext: These operations are empirical and depend on geometric assumptions (same low-error basin, similar architecture). They do not guarantee that the merged model implements a well-defined composition of the source functions.

node_relevance.4 Artifact: STRONG — merged model is the artifact

readjudication_summary: FP-121-006 is a concrete instantiation of weight-space composition but lacks formal semantics. It should not be treated as strict function equivalence.

definition: Function specifications are written as refinement types and verified by SMT. This provides a machine-checkable contract language.
supported_by_fulltext: S120-047 introduces generic refinement types that abstract function contracts; S120-050 uses refinement reflection for complete SMT-based equational verification.
not_supported_by_fulltext: These systems are for pure functional/Haskell/Rust-like programs, not for neural functions or weight-space artifacts. They do not address composition of neural artifacts or probabilistic semantics.

node_relevance.1 FunctionSpec: STRONG — refinement types are formal contracts
node_relevance.2 Representation: PARTIAL — types describe functions, not weights

readjudication_summary: FP-121-007 is essential for GAP-015 but applies to symbolic code, not neural functions. It must be integrated with other paradigms for a full Function OS.

definition: Functions carry effect signatures that are interpreted by handlers at composition/execution time, separating side effects from their implementation.
supported_by_fulltext: S120-053 presents handlers for algebraic effects; S120-055 surveys operational semantics and implementations in Haskell, OCaml, SML, and Racket.
not_supported_by_fulltext: Effect handlers are a language-level feature; they do not directly solve function specification, weight-space composition, or neural function equivalence.

node_relevance.1 FunctionSpec: PARTIAL — effect signature is part of contract

readjudication_summary: FP-121-008 is a strong candidate for GAP-018. It must be adapted to ignition's function representation layer.

definition: Functions are probabilistic programs with operational and denotational semantics, supported by inference and effect handlers.
supported_by_fulltext: S120-058 introduces stochastic probabilities and nested inference; S120-059 gives operational/denotational semantics for higher-order probabilistic programs; S120-064 (Pyro) implements universal probabilistic programming with composable effect handlers.
not_supported_by_fulltext: Probabilistic programming is a semantic framework, not a weight-space composition system. It does not address equivalence of neural artifacts or general function specifications.

node_relevance.1 FunctionSpec: PARTIAL — probabilistic model is a specification
node_relevance.9 VersionedRegistry: PARTIAL — model components can be versioned

readjudication_summary: FP-121-009 is the strongest candidate for GAP-020. It provides a rigorous probabilistic semantics that can be layered onto ignition's function model.

definition: Functions are stored as executable skills in a library, discovered automatically, retrieved by need, and composed to solve new tasks.
supported_by_fulltext: S120-065 (MUSE-Autoskill) creates, stores, and refines skills with a catalog; S120-070 (VOYAGER) maintains an ever-growing skill library and automatically retrieves/composes skills for Minecraft tasks.
not_supported_by_fulltext: Skills are typically LLM-generated code snippets, not formally specified functions. There is no formal equivalence check or effect tracking beyond empirical execution.

node_relevance.4 Artifact: PARTIAL — skill code is the artifact
node_relevance.8 ComposerRouter: STRONG — retrieval and composition are central

readjudication_summary: FP-121-010 is a strong candidate for GAP-019. It demonstrates that a versioned, retrievable, composable function registry can be built and used in practice.
